annotation.interpretation_a: The server can send multiple HTTP messages as a response to a single request if interim responses are sent first.
annotation.interpretation_b: The server might send multiple HTTP messages as a response to a single request if interim responses are sent first, but it is not required to do so.
annotation.justification: The use of 'MAY' creates ambiguity. Does the server have the option to send a single final response even after sending interim responses, or is sending multiple messages mandatory when interim responses are present? This impacts how a client parses and handles the response stream.
annotation.missing_information: The degree of freedom granted by 'MAY' is not constrained. It is unclear if the server *must* send multiple messages when interim responses are present, or if it *can* choose to do so. This affects implementation because a client needs to know if it should expect only one final response even after 1xx responses.
